body.statement: Let \(Q\in R[X_1,\ldots,X_{p_{\mathrm{dim}}}]\) and let \(\mathscr P\) contain at most \(s_{\mathrm{count}}\) polynomials in the same variables, all of degree at most \(D_{\mathrm{deg}}\), over a real closed field \(R\), and let the real dimension of \(\operatorname{Zer}(Q,R^{p_{\mathrm{dim}}})\) be \(p_0\).  There is an algorithm computing a finite set meeting every semialgebraically connected component of every realizable sign condition of \(\mathscr P\) over that zero set in \(s_{\mathrm{count}}^{p_0}D_{\mathrm{deg}}^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}\) ring operations; returning the signs of every polynomial at every sample costs \(s_{\mathrm{count}}^{p_0+1}D_{\mathrm{deg}}^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}\).  The algebraic samples may be recorded by real-univariate representations whose selected roots are specified by Thom encodings.  In particular, taking \(Q=0\) and \(p_0=p_{\mathrm{dim}}\) gives the ambient-space sampling bounds used here.
